stem: Which set identifies the three central Zero Trust principles?

choices.A: Trust the office, share passwords, and disable logging
choices.B: Use one region, one account, and one firewall
choices.C: Verify explicitly, use least privilege, and assume breach
choices.D: Encrypt invoices, reserve capacity, and add tags

explanations.A: These practices undermine verification and containment.
explanations.B: Those are infrastructure choices rather than the principles.
explanations.C: These principles guide Zero Trust access design.
explanations.D: These do not define Zero Trust principles.

stem: A user is connected to the office network. How should a Zero Trust design treat the request?

choices.A: Verify identity and context before authorizing access
choices.B: Disable monitoring for the request
choices.C: Skip authentication because the network is internal
choices.D: Give the user subscription Owner

explanations.A: Network location alone is insufficient evidence of trust.
explanations.B: Monitoring remains useful for detecting compromise.
explanations.C: Internal networks can also contain compromised systems.
explanations.D: Location does not justify broad privileges.

stem: What does least privilege mean for a help-desk task?

choices.A: Avoid assigning any identity to workloads
choices.B: Require every user to manage all tenant policies
choices.C: Grant the minimum permission needed at the appropriate scope
choices.D: Give every employee identical administrator rights

explanations.A: Workloads still need authenticated identities.
explanations.B: That expands privileges beyond most tasks.
explanations.C: Access should match the job rather than exceed it.
explanations.D: Jobs have different permission needs.

stem: What does assume breach encourage an architect to do?

choices.A: Limit lateral movement and detect suspicious activity
choices.B: Assume an internal network cannot be attacked
choices.C: Make application data public to simplify troubleshooting
choices.D: Remove backups because prevention is sufficient

explanations.A: The design accounts for an attacker already having a foothold.
explanations.B: That conflicts with the principle.
explanations.C: That increases exposure.
explanations.D: Recovery remains necessary.

stem: A temporary contractor needs to read one report store. Which design best reflects Zero Trust?

choices.A: Give narrowly scoped access for the required task and review its lifetime
choices.B: Share the database administrator password
choices.C: Disable authentication on the store
choices.D: Grant permanent subscription Owner

explanations.A: Scope and duration reduce unnecessary exposure.
explanations.B: Shared secrets weaken verification and accountability.
explanations.C: Removing identity checks does not implement Zero Trust.
explanations.D: That exceeds the task.

stem: Why does Zero Trust use device and risk context with identity information?

choices.A: It guarantees no attack can succeed
choices.B: It removes the need for any authorization
choices.C: The access decision benefits from more evidence than a username
choices.D: It ensures every device is physically in one datacenter

explanations.A: Security strategies reduce risk rather than guarantee perfection.
explanations.B: Permission checks still matter.
explanations.C: Additional signals help verify the request explicitly.
explanations.D: Zero Trust is not a physical-placement requirement.

stem: An application is compromised. Which design can reduce the damage to unrelated systems?

choices.A: Disabling resource activity logs
choices.B: A shared highly privileged identity for all apps
choices.C: Segmentation with limited workload permissions
choices.D: One unrestricted internal network

explanations.A: That makes investigation harder.
explanations.B: That expands cross-system exposure.
explanations.C: Containment reduces the potential blast radius.
explanations.D: Unrestricted movement helps an attacker.

stem: Which request should be evaluated under Zero Trust?

choices.A: Only guest users requesting expensive services
choices.B: Both internal and external access requests
choices.C: Only requests made from PowerShell
choices.D: Only traffic originating outside the country

explanations.A: Employees and other requests also require verification.
explanations.B: Trust should not be assumed solely from network location.
explanations.C: The client tool does not define the trust model.
explanations.D: Country alone does not define all relevant risk.

stem: A team removes standing administrator access and grants privileged access only when needed. Which principle does this support?

choices.A: Least privilege
choices.B: Verify explicitly
choices.C: Assume breach
choices.D: Perimeter-based trust

explanations.A: Reducing privilege scope and lifetime supports minimal access.
explanations.B: Explicit verification evaluates identity and context; the stated change primarily limits privilege lifetime.
explanations.C: Assuming breach guides containment and detection; limiting standing administrator access directly implements least privilege.
explanations.D: Trust based mainly on network location conflicts with Zero Trust and does not describe time-limited privilege.

stem: What is an accurate statement about Zero Trust implementation?

choices.A: It requires making every resource private regardless of its purpose
choices.B: It combines policies, identities, devices, and other protections
choices.C: Buying one firewall completes the strategy
choices.D: It eliminates the customer share of security responsibility

explanations.A: Controls should follow requirements and risk.
explanations.B: It is a strategy applied across multiple control areas.
explanations.C: A single product cannot cover all principles.
explanations.D: Customers still configure access and protect data.

stem: Why use defense in depth?

choices.A: To make every layer use the same password
choices.B: Several layers can limit harm when one control fails
choices.C: To avoid monitoring after a firewall is installed
choices.D: To replace all application security with physical locks

explanations.A: Shared credentials weaken the layers.
explanations.B: Layering reduces dependence on one protection.
explanations.C: Monitoring complements preventive controls.
explanations.D: Application threats need application protections.

stem: Which example represents protections at different layers?

choices.A: MFA for identities, network filtering, and data encryption
choices.B: Three IP filtering rules with no identity or data controls
choices.C: Three MFA methods with no host or application protections
choices.D: Three backups with no authentication or application protections

explanations.A: These address identity, network, and data risks.
explanations.B: These remain concentrated in the network layer.
explanations.C: Those focus on identity rather than different defensive layers.
explanations.D: Recovery copies do not provide the requested spread of preventive layers.

stem: A public web app needs anonymous access to its home page. What remains useful in a layered design?

choices.A: Secure application code, protected administration, and monitored data access
choices.B: Removing all TLS encryption
choices.C: Anonymous administrator access
choices.D: Storing secrets in the home-page source

explanations.A: Public content does not require unprotected management or data.
explanations.B: Public-facing traffic still benefits from TLS.
explanations.C: Administration should remain protected.
explanations.D: Public source must not expose secrets.

stem: Which security layer addresses unauthorized access to physical server hardware in Azure datacenters?

choices.A: Application input validation
choices.B: Physical security
choices.C: Azure RBAC
choices.D: Sensitivity labels

explanations.A: That protects application processing.
explanations.B: Provider controls protect the physical facilities.
explanations.C: That authorizes resource operations.
explanations.D: Those help classify and protect information.

stem: What is the role of encryption at rest in a defense-in-depth design?

choices.A: Replace identity verification
choices.B: Protect stored data if underlying storage is accessed improperly
choices.C: Authorize users to modify every resource
choices.D: Guarantee that malicious code cannot run

explanations.A: Access still requires appropriate identity controls.
explanations.B: Encryption addresses a data-protection layer.
explanations.C: Authorization is separate.
explanations.D: Encryption is not a code-execution prevention guarantee.

stem: A firewall is configured correctly, but a user exposes data with excessive permissions. What does this show?

choices.A: Network protection cannot substitute for access control
choices.B: Encryption at rest is impossible in Azure
choices.C: A firewall always grants least privilege
choices.D: Azure regions determine every user's permissions

explanations.A: Different threats require different protective layers.
explanations.B: The incident says nothing about encryption availability.
explanations.C: Firewalls do not automatically scope user roles.
explanations.D: Roles and application controls determine permissions.

stem: Which control helps detect a failure of preventive defenses?

choices.A: Naming every resource identically
choices.B: Disabling identity checks
choices.C: Removing all audit records
choices.D: Monitoring and alerting

explanations.A: Naming does not detect attacks.
explanations.B: That creates additional risk.
explanations.C: That reduces visibility.
explanations.D: Detection helps identify suspicious behavior after access occurs.

stem: A learner describes defense in depth as installing two identical firewalls and stopping there. What is missing?

choices.A: A stricter resource naming convention alone
choices.B: Additional copies of the same perimeter firewall rule alone
choices.C: A larger firewall VM SKU alone
choices.D: Protection across identity, application, data, and other layers

explanations.A: Names do not provide the missing security layers.
explanations.B: That does not address missing identity, host, application, and data controls.
explanations.C: More capacity in one layer is not broad defensive coverage.
explanations.D: Depth spans complementary controls rather than only one control type.

stem: Which pair best separates prevention from recovery?

choices.A: Access restrictions reduce exposure; tested backups support restoration
choices.B: Tags prevent malware; DNS records restore databases
choices.C: Invoices prevent phishing; budgets recover deleted files
choices.D: Azure regions authenticate users; MFA restores disks

explanations.A: Both activities contribute to resilient defense.
explanations.B: These claims assign the wrong capabilities.
explanations.C: Billing tools do not perform those functions.
explanations.D: Those functions are mismatched.

stem: How does patching a customer-managed guest operating system contribute to layered security?

choices.A: It changes a subscription into a tenant
choices.B: It automatically grants application data permissions
choices.C: It removes the need for network segmentation
choices.D: It reduces exposure to known software vulnerabilities

explanations.A: Patching does not alter identity or billing boundaries.
explanations.B: Patching does not assign data roles.
explanations.C: Complementary network controls still matter.
explanations.D: VM guest maintenance is a useful host-level control.

stem: What is a main purpose of Microsoft Defender for Cloud?

choices.A: Host every application database
choices.B: Provide a replacement for every Azure billing tool
choices.C: Calculate only network address ranges
choices.D: Assess security posture and provide workload-protection capabilities

explanations.A: It does not serve as a universal database host.
explanations.B: It is a security service.
explanations.C: Address planning is not its core purpose.
explanations.D: It helps identify and address cloud security risks.

stem: An administrator wants a prioritized view of configuration weaknesses across cloud resources. Which service should be evaluated?

choices.A: Azure Pricing Calculator
choices.B: Microsoft Defender for Cloud
choices.C: Azure DNS
choices.D: Azure Data Box

explanations.A: The calculator estimates costs.
explanations.B: Its posture capabilities help identify security weaknesses.
explanations.C: DNS resolves names.
explanations.D: Data Box is for offline data movement.

stem: What should a team do before enabling a Defender workload-protection plan in a learning subscription?

choices.A: Assume every plan is always free
choices.B: Enable it in every subscription automatically
choices.C: Review scope, permissions, and current pricing
choices.D: Publish credentials to prove the plan works

explanations.A: Pricing varies by capability and plan.
explanations.B: The lab does not authorize broad paid activation.
explanations.C: Plan activation can add charges and affect the selected scope.
explanations.D: Credentials must remain private.

stem: A security recommendation reports excessive exposure. What is the appropriate next step?

choices.A: Ignore it because Azure owns physical security
choices.B: Treat the finding as proof that compliance is complete
choices.C: Delete every resource in the tenant
choices.D: Investigate the finding and plan a tested remediation

explanations.A: Customer configuration still affects exposure.
explanations.B: A recommendation identifies work rather than certification.
explanations.C: That is disproportionate and destructive.
explanations.D: Recommendations need contextual review before changes.

stem: Which distinction is useful when learning Defender for Cloud?

choices.A: Posture assessment identifies risks; workload protection helps detect threats
choices.B: Posture assessment guarantees compliance; workload protection guarantees no breach
choices.C: Posture assessment approves resource access; workload protection assigns Azure roles
choices.D: Posture assessment estimates billing; workload protection sets budgets

explanations.A: These capabilities address related but distinct security needs.
explanations.B: Neither capability supplies those universal guarantees.
explanations.C: Resource authorization still requires deliberate role and access design.
explanations.D: Those are cost-management functions.

stem: How should a beginner interpret a favorable security score?

choices.A: As permission to remove application authentication
choices.B: As one input for prioritizing security improvements
choices.C: As legal proof of every regulatory obligation
choices.D: As a guarantee that no breach can occur

explanations.A: Authentication remains necessary.
explanations.B: A score summarizes measured posture and has limits.
explanations.C: Regulatory compliance needs broader evidence.
explanations.D: No posture score guarantees prevention.

stem: A team uses resources in Azure and another cloud. Which security need can Defender for Cloud address?

choices.A: Free migration of every database
choices.B: A consolidated view of supported multicloud security posture
choices.C: A guarantee of identical features for every provider
choices.D: Automatic deletion of every external server

explanations.A: Security assessment is not a universal migration service.
explanations.B: Supported connected environments can contribute to the posture view.
explanations.C: Capabilities and onboarding requirements can differ.
explanations.D: That is not its purpose.

stem: Why might an organization combine Defender recommendations with its own threat model?

choices.A: A threat model disables Defender billing
choices.B: Recommendations automatically know every business requirement
choices.C: The workload's context affects remediation priorities
choices.D: Resource tags fully prevent attacks

explanations.A: Pricing is not changed by the document.
explanations.B: They do not replace contextual analysis.
explanations.C: Business purpose and architecture matter alongside findings.
explanations.D: Tags are not threat-prevention controls.

stem: A learner wants to complete this security lab without changing any subscription security plans. Which activity fits?

choices.A: Analyze labeled synthetic findings and map controls to them
choices.B: Install agents on production servers
choices.C: Enable all paid Defender plans
choices.D: Create a tenant-wide privileged role assignment

explanations.A: Concept exercises meet the learning goal without plan activation.
explanations.B: That is operational onboarding.
explanations.C: That changes configuration and may incur charges.
explanations.D: That modifies real access outside the lab.

stem: Which conclusion follows from using Defender for Cloud?

choices.A: All data becomes publicly discoverable
choices.B: Every Azure resource becomes immune to attacks
choices.C: The customer no longer manages identities
choices.D: The customer still needs to act on appropriate findings and maintain protections

explanations.A: Security posture management does not make data public.
explanations.B: Security services cannot guarantee immunity.
explanations.C: Identity responsibility remains.
explanations.D: The service supports security work rather than transferring all duties.
